findings.claim: The caller workflow template passes `folders: docs` and filters on `docs/**` only. That overrides the openviking-sync action's default (`docs` and `.okf`) and differs from this repo's own `.github/workflows/openviking-sync.yaml`, and the skill never asks which folders to sync. A repository with a `.okf/` bundle, such as one using kmctl, gets it silently left out of OpenViking. Ask the operator which folders to sync. Drop `folders:` when the answer is the action's default, and build the `paths` filter from the same list.

Step 5 says the push must come first because 'the action change must be on GitHub first'. Onboarding changes no action: the lab-auth and openviking-sync actions are already on origin/main. The real reasons to push first are that the pinned SHA must exist on GitHub and main should match what was applied. Reword the sentence.

test_default_callers compares a list in Terraform's map order, which sorts by key. The skill says 'add the new caller' without saying that the entry goes in key order, so a repo whose name sorts before `loop-engineering-harness` fails the test when appended. The step 3.4 test run catches it, so this costs a retry and nothing more. Say 'in key order'.

verdict.text: The skill is correct where it counts.

An agent following it ends up with an applied onboarding: lab Environment, a `vault_ci_callers` entry, the prefix map, the exact-list tests, two applies from saved and checked plans, a `vault read` check, commit through the loop, a push only after asking, and a pinned caller workflow with no Tailscale inputs.
The expected-plan list matches every resource keyed on `var.vault_ci_callers`.
Three non-blocking fixes remain.
The one that matters is f1: the caller template narrows the synced folders to `docs` without asking.
Gates: `loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree, stamp green `eabd7f93...2020`.
pre_commit, cli_tests, and rows r1, r2 and r3 pass.
r1: the test runs `git check-ignore -q` on the file and asserts exit code 1, then checks the front matter name and description.
I confirmed by hand that `git check-ignore -v` ignores `.claude/skills/foo/SKILL.md` and not the onboard-repo one, and that the `.claude/rules` exceptions still hold.
r2: the test collects backticked tokens that contain `/` and end in an extension or `/`, and asserts each exists.
Placeholders with `<>`, `$SCRATCH` paths and ARNs fall outside the pattern, as they should.
A misspelled real path would fail it.
r3: the test parses the single yaml block that names `lab-auth@`.
It asserts no pull_request or pull_request_target, `id-token: write`, `environment: lab`, `with` keys within each action's declared inputs, and no Tailscale inputs.
That covers fails_when.
r4 (judgment): passes.
The skill forbids `just apply` and a bare `terraform apply`, and the reason it gives matches both justfiles (`terraform apply -var-file=...` re-plans and prompts).
It saves with `-out` and applies only that file.
It stops and shows the operator anything outside the expected list for both roots, and it never pipes `yes`.
r5 (judgment): passes.
Every step in the plan's intent is there.
The how-to links the skill under Additional resources, and the four-section skeleton is unchanged.

The expected plan, checked against code: `vault_jwt_auth_backend_role.github_ci` (machine_roles.tf, for_each on the variable); `vault_identity_oidc_role.ci_ov_sync` (oidc.tf) and `vault_policy.ci_ov_sync` (machine_roles.tf), both limited to ov_sync callers; `nomad_job.seaweedfs` through `local.seaweedfs_ci_callers` and `seaweedfs_iam` (policy and role `ci-<key>`, resource `arn:aws:s3:::ov-sync/<repo>/*`); `null_resource.firewall` with `always_run = timestamp()` in infrastructure only.
The applications firewall and bifrost_ready have no always-changing triggers, so "only `nomad_job.ov_sync_consumer`" is right.
No other resource reads the variable.
`192.168.2.29:8333` is SeaweedFS's S3 and IAM port, which the applications aws provider reads through Consul.
`uv run localstack env` works from `deployments/applications`.
`vault read auth/jwt-github/role/<key>` matches the mount, and the bound_claims are the four named.
ADR 0031 and lab-auth's `tailscale-identity` step: no Tailscale inputs are needed for either subject format.
The `route-ask` skill exists in the loop-harness plugin.
f1: the `folders: docs` override and the `docs/**`-only paths filter, explained above.
This is a design choice the skill makes for the operator without asking.
f2: a false reason for pushing first.
f3: the order of the exact list is not stated.
It is self-correcting through the test run.
Step 4's commands share `cd`, `eval` and `$SCRATCH` across code blocks.
An agent whose shell resets between calls has to re-run `eval "$(uv run localstack env)"` and spell out its scratchpad path.
The skill's 403 note covers the expired-token case, so I am not raising it as a finding.
